h: Red rooms, rare motors and a good long lunch
p: One part that tends to stop people in their tracks is the famous Red Room, packed with cars in every shade of red you can imagine. It's a photographer's dream and a bit of a sensory overload in the best way. Elsewhere you'll find themed displays covering everything from British classics to American muscle and the great racing names, so even if your interest in cars starts and ends with "the shiny one", there's plenty to grab you.

How long to allow? Half a day is a sensible minimum, and many visitors stay most of the day, especially if the kids get stuck into the activities or you stop for a proper sit-down meal. The restaurant is popular with A303 travellers, which tells you it does the job well.

Petrolheads will want to read every display panel, while younger children often enjoy spotting cars they recognise from films and cartoons. It's a lovely place to bring three generations together, as older relatives inevitably start telling stories about the cars they owned, crashed or courted in.
Handy tips: wear comfy shoes, as the halls cover a fair bit of ground, and keep an eye on the event calendar, because special days and car club gatherings can add an extra layer of fun.

If you've got time afterwards, the market town of Castle Cary and the hilltop viewpoint at Cadbury Castle, linked in legend with King Arthur's Camelot, are both close by, and the Fleet Air Arm Museum at Yeovilton is only a short drive along the A303 for a transport-themed weekend.
